label: HTTP route
description: A route. The body is decoded by the consumes codec into request.body (typed by settings.body); query, route placeholders (request.params, each one required), headers and the principal are in the context too. The trigger's input mapping picks what the graph gets; access is checked before the graph runs; the answer is encoded by the produces codec with the status the response block chooses. A refusal (a graph ending on purpose with a reason) is answered as { reason, message } with the status response.refusals maps that reason to; every reason the route can reach must be mapped (T005). A fault is a 500.

route.description: e.g. /tasks or /tasks/{id}; each {name} is a required request.params.name

consumes.description: the body's content type; must be in the plugin's codecs table

produces.description: the answer's content type; must be in the codecs table. Default application/json

body.description: the edge type of the decoded body (request.body); declaring it means a body is expected, so a request without one is a 400. Absent: the body is the trigger's in

roles.description: the principal must hold one of these

access.description: absent: a valid token is required, any role

from.description: a path into the answer whose value picks the status

status.description: the status of an answer: from a path into it through map, else default (200)

refusals.description: reason -> status: how each refusal the route can reach is answered, e.g. { "missing": 404, "upstream": 502 }. The body is { reason, message }.

response.description: how the route answers: the status of an answer, and one status per refusal reason

params.description: the route's placeholders, each a string the route guarantees
